experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður
experiences.description: Join a guided northern lights tour departing from Siglufjörður, venturing into the dark fjordside countryside away from light pollution. The remote location of Siglufjörður in northern Iceland makes it one of the best spots in the country to witness the aurora borealis dancing over the fjord and surrounding mountains.

experiences.name: Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool
experiences.description: Visit the stunning Hofsós swimming pool, often called Iceland's most beautiful geothermal pool, perched on a cliff edge overlooking Skagafjörður fjord. A short scenic drive from Siglufjörður, this geothermally heated outdoor pool offers breathtaking panoramic views of the fjord and distant mountains, especially magical at sunset or under the northern lights.

experiences.name: Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike
experiences.description: Explore the hauntingly beautiful and completely uninhabited Héðinsfjörður fjord, accessible via a short tunnel from Siglufjörður. Hike through this remote valley to discover the ruins of an abandoned fishing village, dramatic waterfalls, and pristine Arctic nature. The fjord is surrounded by towering peaks and offers exceptional wildlife spotting including Arctic foxes and seabirds.

experiences.name: Herring Era Museum & Local Culture Experience
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Siglufjörður's rich cultural heritage at the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið), one of Iceland's finest regional museums. Explore restored warehouses and boats that tell the story of the great herring boom of the early 20th century. Pair the visit with a meal at a local restaurant sampling traditional Icelandic fish dishes and lamb soup.

experiences.name: Tröllaskagi Peninsula Whale Watching & Sea Safari
experiences.description: Embark on a sea safari from the nearby town of Dalvík or Ólafsfjörður, exploring the rich marine waters of Eyjafjörður — one of Iceland's longest fjords. These waters are home to humpback whales, minke whales, white-beaked dolphins, and harbour porpoises. The dramatic mountain scenery of the Tröllaskagi Peninsula provides a stunning backdrop for this unforgettable Arctic wildlife experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike
experiences.description: Explore the hauntingly beautiful and completely uninhabited Héðinsfjörður fjord, accessible via a short tunnel from Siglufjörður. Hike through this remote valley to discover the ruins of an abandoned fishing village, dramatic waterfalls, and pristine Arctic nature. The fjord is surrounded by towering peaks and offers exceptional wildlife spotting including Arctic foxes and seabirds.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or a budget shuttle to Reykjavik BSI terminal (approx. 3,000 ISK). Store luggage at BSI or a nearby locker while you wait for onward travel. Grab a coffee and warm up at the terminal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a long-distance bus or arrange a pre-booked budget car rental for the scenic drive north toward Siglufjörður (approx. 5–6 hours including stops). Stop at Borgarnes service station for a cheap meal and stretch your legs. Continue through the Hvalfjörður tunnel and along Route 1 northward.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður by early evening. Check in, unpack, and settle into your room. Take a short stroll along the quiet harbor front to get your bearings in this charming fishing town. Return to the hotel to rest after the long travel day. Keep an eye on the sky after 21:00 for any early northern lights activity — January darkness in Siglufjörður begins around 16:00, giving excellent aurora-watching windows.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at Keflavik Airport before or after landing (budget ~1,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Borgarnes service station — soup of the day or a hot dog (classic Icelandic budget staple, ~1,200 ISK)
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — a cozy local café offering affordable fish soup and sandwiches (~2,500–3,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January sunrise in Siglufjörður is around 11:30 and sunset around 15:30, so daylight is very limited. Dress in warm layers — temperatures around 0–5°C with possible wind and rain. Download the Vedur.is app for weather and aurora forecasts. If renting a car, ensure it has winter tires (mandatory in Iceland in winter).

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, visit the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) in Siglufjörður — one of Iceland's best regional museums, documenting the town's booming herring industry. Entry is around 2,000 ISK and well worth it. The museum is a short walk from Hotel Siglunes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or hike the short distance to the trailhead for the Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike. Cross the short tunnel (Héðinsfjarðargöng) to reach the hauntingly beautiful and completely uninhabited Héðinsfjörður fjord. Explore the ruins of the old farmsteads and soak in the dramatic, desolate winter landscape. The fjord is surrounded by steep mountains and the silence is extraordinary. Keep the hike moderate given winter conditions — stay on marked paths and return before darkness falls around 15:30.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður before dark. Warm up with a hot drink at the hotel. After dinner, bundle up and head to the harbor or a dark hillside above town for northern lights watching — Siglufjörður's remote location and minimal light pollution make it one of the best spots in Iceland for aurora viewing. Check aurora forecast on Vedur.is (aim for KP index 2+ and clear skies).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or self-catered oats and fruit from a local shop (~500–800 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade sandwich and thermos of hot soup from the hotel or local Krónan/Bónus supermarket (~600 ISK)
meals.dinner: Sægreifinn-style budget fish stew cooked in your room if kitchen available, or Kaffi Rauðka for a warm bowl of lamb soup (~2,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Héðinsfjörður is accessible via the Héðinsfjarðargöng tunnel — check that it is open in winter conditions before setting out. Wear waterproof boots and crampons/ice cleats as paths may be icy. Bring a headlamp. The hike is free of charge.

day_by_day.morning: Take a leisurely morning walk around Siglufjörður town. Visit the colorful harbor and watch local fishing boats. Pop into the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) — Icelandic public pools are a budget traveler's dream at around 1,000–1,200 ISK entry. Soak in the geothermally heated outdoor hot pots and warm up completely.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive east along Route 76 toward Ólafsfjörður (about 20 minutes through the twin tunnels). Explore this smaller, quieter fishing village. Walk along the fjord shore and enjoy the dramatic mountain scenery. Visit the local church and wander the peaceful streets. Return to Siglufjörður by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights vigil from the hillside above Siglufjörður. The town sits in a deep fjord, so climbing slightly above the town gives a wider sky view. Bring a tripod if you have a camera. Alternatively, relax at the hotel with a book and check the aurora forecast every hour, stepping outside when conditions look promising.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: skyr with granola and coffee (~500 ISK from local shop)
meals.lunch: Hot dog from a local petrol station or bakery in Ólafsfjörður (~400–600 ISK) — a true Icelandic budget tradition
meals.dinner: Cook a simple pasta or rice dish in the hotel kitchen if available, or pick up a ready meal from the local Samkaup supermarket in Siglufjörður (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Siglufjörður swimming pool is a fantastic budget activity and a great way to meet locals. Towel rental is usually available for a small fee. Check pool opening hours in advance as they may vary in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along Route 76 and then Route 1 toward Akureyri (Iceland's second city, about 1.5 hours from Siglufjörður). Arrive in Akureyri mid-morning. Visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church — entry is free and the views over the fjord from the steps are stunning even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Akureyri on foot. Browse the pedestrian shopping street (Hafnarstræti) for budget souvenirs. Visit the Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri) — entry is around 1,500 ISK. Walk along the fjord waterfront. Stop at the famous heart-shaped traffic lights, unique to Akureyri. Visit the Bónus supermarket to stock up on budget groceries for the coming days.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Siglufjörður, stopping at a dark pullout along Route 1 or Route 76 for northern lights watching on the way back. The drive along Eyjafjörður offers wide open skies away from city light pollution. Return to the hotel by 21:00.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before departure (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Akureyri Backpackers café or Bláa Kannan café on Hafnarstræti — soup and bread deal (~1,800–2,200 ISK)
meals.dinner: Grocery store haul from Bónus in Akureyri — cook a hearty meal at the hotel (~1,200–1,500 ISK for ingredients)

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is the cultural hub of northern Iceland and worth a half-day visit. The drive back via Route 76 hugs dramatic fjord scenery. Fill up your rental car in Akureyri as fuel is cheaper in larger towns than in remote areas.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. This is a good day to do laundry at the hotel or a local laundromat. Spend time planning the rest of the trip, updating travel notes, and reviewing aurora forecasts for the week ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Siglufjörður area on foot. Walk the perimeter of the town along the fjord shore. Look for seabirds along the waterfront — eider ducks and other winter seabirds are common. Visit the small local library or community center to warm up and use free WiFi.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated northern lights evening. Check Vedur.is for aurora and cloud forecasts. If conditions are favorable (clear skies, KP 2+), drive a few kilometers out of town along Route 76 to escape any residual town glow. Park safely and watch the sky. January in northern Iceland offers up to 18 hours of darkness — ideal aurora conditions.

meals.breakfast: Homemade pancakes or eggs cooked at hotel (~400 ISK in ingredients)
meals.lunch: Leftovers from previous night's grocery cook-up, or a simple skyr and fruit (~300 ISK)
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka or local restaurant — treat yourself to a slightly larger meal as a mid-trip reward (~3,000–3,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: A rest day is important on a 13-day trip, especially in harsh winter conditions. Use this day to recharge physically and mentally. January weather in Siglufjörður can be unpredictable — a rest day also provides buffer for weather delays.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east from Siglufjörður along Route 76 and then Route 1 toward Lake Mývatn (approximately 2.5–3 hours). Arrive at Mývatn mid-morning. Visit the Námaskarð geothermal area (Hverir) — a surreal landscape of bubbling mud pots, steaming fumaroles, and sulfurous vents. Entry is free and the area is otherworldly, especially in winter with possible snow and steam.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mývatn area further. Visit the Dimmuborgir lava formations — a free, dramatic landscape of twisted lava pillars and caves formed by an ancient lava lake. Walk the marked trails (wear ice cleats). Then visit Skútustaðagígar pseudo-craters along the lake shore — also free and fascinating geological features.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a budget guesthouse or hostel near Mývatn for the night (pre-booked — options include Vogafjós Guesthouse or Mývatn Hostel, approx. 8,000–12,000 ISK for a dorm or budget room). After dinner, head to a dark spot near the lake for northern lights watching — Mývatn's remote location makes it excellent for aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Siglufjörður hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and a thermos for the road and Mývatn exploration (~600 ISK)
meals.dinner: Vogafjós Farm Restaurant near Mývatn — known for affordable geothermal bread and local lamb soup (~2,500–3,000 ISK), or self-cater from Reykjahlíð village shop

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn is one of Iceland's most geologically active and visually stunning areas. The Námaskarð area smells strongly of sulfur — completely normal. Wear sturdy waterproof boots as the ground can be muddy and icy. This is an overnight away from Hotel Siglunes — confirm your hotel allows this flexibility or that you have a flexible booking.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a geothermal lagoon similar to the Blue Lagoon but far less crowded and more affordable (entry approx. 5,500 ISK). Soak in the milky blue, mineral-rich waters surrounded by volcanic landscape. This is a highlight of any Iceland trip and perfect for a cold January morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Goðafoss waterfall (about 30 minutes west of Mývatn on Route 1) — one of Iceland's most beautiful waterfalls, free to visit. The falls are dramatic year-round but especially atmospheric in winter with ice formations along the edges. Spend an hour exploring the viewpoints on both sides of the river.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður (approximately 2–2.5 hours). Arrive by early evening. Unpack and relax. Check aurora forecast and head out for northern lights watching if conditions are favorable.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast if included, or self-catered (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Goðafoss viewpoint — thermos of soup and sandwiches (~600 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at Hotel Siglunes using groceries stocked up earlier (~1,200 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Mývatn Nature Baths are significantly cheaper than the Blue Lagoon and far less touristy — highly recommended. Book tickets online in advance to guarantee entry. Goðafoss is free and accessible year-round but the parking area may be icy — park carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Siglufjörður swimming pool for a relaxing soak in the hot pots. This is a great way to interact with locals and warm up after a busy week. Spend 1–2 hours at the pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive along Route 76 to explore the Tröllaskagi peninsula coastline. Stop at scenic viewpoints overlooking the fjords and mountains. Visit the small village of Hofsós (about 45 minutes from Siglufjörður) — home to the Icelandic Emigration Center (Vesturfarasetrið), which documents Icelandic emigration to North America. Entry is around 1,500 ISK. The village also has a stunning infinity-edge swimming pool overlooking Skagafjörður (check winter opening hours).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Cook a hearty dinner at the hotel. Spend the evening aurora watching — by now you'll have a good feel for the best local spots and how to read the forecast.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: oatmeal with skyr and berries (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Hofsós village — bring a packed lunch or grab a snack at the local petrol station (~500–800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered: Icelandic lamb stew made with ingredients from Bónus (~1,500 ISK for a hearty pot)

day_by_day.notes: The Hofsós swimming pool is one of Iceland's most scenic public pools with views over the fjord — check winter opening hours carefully as it may have reduced hours. The Tröllaskagi peninsula drive is spectacular even in winter with snow-capped mountains.

day_by_day.morning: Take a winter nature walk in the hills immediately above Siglufjörður. The terrain is accessible on foot from the hotel. Enjoy panoramic views over the fjord and town below. Look for ptarmigan (Icelandic grouse) which are common in winter hillsides and turn completely white for camouflage. Bring binoculars if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Museum annex buildings — the museum complex includes several restored herring-era buildings along the harbor. Spend the afternoon exploring at your own pace. Alternatively, use the afternoon for a longer drive along Route 76 toward Sauðárkrókur to see more of the Skagafjörður region.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated photography and aurora evening. Set up at the harbor or hillside above town. The harbor reflections can make for stunning aurora photography if the lights appear. Even without aurora, the winter night sky over Siglufjörður is spectacular with minimal light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or self-catered (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Thermos of hot chocolate and packed sandwiches on the hillside walk (~400 ISK)
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka — fish and chips or daily special (~2,500–3,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Winter hillside walks above Siglufjörður require caution — avalanche risk exists in some areas after heavy snowfall. Check local conditions and do not venture onto steep slopes after significant snowfall. Stick to established paths.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south toward Varmahlíð in Skagafjörður (about 1 hour from Siglufjörður). Visit the Glaumbær turf farm museum — one of Iceland's best-preserved traditional turf farmhouses, offering a fascinating glimpse into how Icelanders lived for centuries. Entry is around 2,000 ISK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Skagafjörður area. Visit the Víðimýrarkirkja turf church near Varmahlíð — a beautifully preserved 19th-century turf church, free to view from outside. Drive along the Skagafjörður valley, one of Iceland's most scenic agricultural regions even in winter. Return to Siglufjörður via Route 75 and Route 76.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel. Review photos from the trip so far. Check aurora forecast and head out if conditions are good. This is one of your last evenings in the area — make the most of the dark skies.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before departure (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Café at Glaumbær museum or packed lunch in the car (~1,500–2,000 ISK at café, or ~600 ISK self-catered)
meals.dinner: Self-catered: pasta with canned fish and vegetables (~1,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær is one of Iceland's most authentic historical sites and well worth the entry fee. The turf buildings are remarkably well preserved. Check opening hours in advance as winter hours may be reduced.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning swim at the Siglufjörður public pool — a fitting farewell to this wonderful local institution. Soak in the hot pots and enjoy the mountain views one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack and check out of Hotel Siglunes. Begin the drive south toward Reykjavik (approximately 5–6 hours). Stop at Blönduós for fuel and a snack. Continue along Route 1 through the dramatic Icelandic interior highlands landscape. Stop at Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls near Reykholt if time permits (free, about 30 minutes off Route 1).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Reykjavik. Check into a budget hostel (Reykjavik City Hostel or KEX Hostel — dorm beds from 5,000–7,000 ISK per night). Explore the Laugavegur street area in the evening. Grab dinner in the city.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at Hotel Siglunes using remaining groceries
meals.lunch: Blönduós petrol station — hot dog and coffee (~600 ISK)
meals.dinner: Reykjavik — Hlöllabátar (Icelandic submarine sandwiches) or Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dog stand (~800–1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Siglufjörður to Reykjavik is long — start no later than 10:00 to arrive comfortably before dark. Route 1 in January can have icy sections — drive carefully and check road conditions on road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavik on foot. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church — the exterior is free, and the tower elevator costs around 1,000 ISK for panoramic city views. Walk down Skólavörðustígur to Laugavegur. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall exterior (free) and walk along the harbor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an underground museum built around a Viking-age longhouse discovered beneath the city, entry around 2,200 ISK. Alternatively, visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) for a comprehensive overview of Icelandic history (entry ~2,000 ISK). Browse the Kolaportið flea market if it's open (weekends only — check if applicable) for cheap Icelandic souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Final northern lights attempt from Reykjavik. The city has light pollution but Grótta lighthouse on the Seltjarnarnes peninsula (a short drive or long walk from the city center) is a popular and accessible aurora-watching spot. Alternatively, join a free or low-cost aurora walking tour from the city center.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast if included, or Sandholt Bakery on Laugavegur for a pastry and coffee (~1,200 ISK)
meals.lunch: Reykjavik Roasters café or a bakery — soup and bread (~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) on the harbor — famous for lobster soup at around 1,800 ISK, one of Reykjavik's best budget dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: Reykjavik is significantly more expensive than Siglufjörður for food and activities — stick to budget options and self-catering where possible. The Sægreifinn lobster soup is legendary and genuinely affordable for what you get.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Check out of the hostel and store luggage. Take a quick walk along the Reykjavik harbor waterfront. Visit the Sun Voyager sculpture (Sólfar) — free and iconic. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs from the Bónus supermarket (Icelandic chocolate, dried fish, and skyr are great budget gifts).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Keflavik International Airport via the Flybus from BSI terminal (book in advance, approx. 3,000 ISK). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the bus journey and airport check-in. Arrive at the airport and complete check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland on your Icelandair flight. Reflect on 13 incredible days of northern lights, hot springs, dramatic fjords, and authentic Icelandic culture — all on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or self-catered: final Icelandic skyr and coffee (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Keflavik Airport — bring snacks from the supermarket to avoid expensive airport food, or budget for a simple airport meal (~2,000–2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport food before departure

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your Flybus departure time from BSI based on your flight time — the Flybus website has a calculator. Arrive at the airport at least 2 hours before departure. Duty-free at Keflavik is one of the cheapest places to buy Icelandic spirits and chocolate — worth a browse on the way out.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage, then arrange a pre-booked rental car or airport transfer. Begin the scenic drive north toward Siglufjörður (approximately 4–5 hours via Route 1 and the Héðinsfjörður tunnel). Stop at a petrol station café near Borgarnes for a warm drink and stretch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive north through the dramatic Tröllaskagi Peninsula. Pass through the Strákagöng and Héðinsfjörður tunnels, arriving in Siglufjörður in the early afternoon. Check in to Hotel Siglunes on Lækjargata 10, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation stroll along the harbour front to get your bearings in this charming fishing town.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Siglufjörður with a relaxed first evening. Head to Hannes Boy restaurant (one of the town's most beloved spots) for a warming bowl of lamb soup or fresh fish of the day. Afterward, step outside to scan the sky — January darkness arrives early and the northern lights can appear on clear nights even from the town harbour.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at the airport or a roadside petrol station café (Orkan or N1) en route north — budget around 1,500–2,000 ISK.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple sandwich from a Bonus or Krónan supermarket in Akureyri if passing through, or stop at a roadside diner on Route 1 — budget around 2,000–3,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður — cosy atmosphere, locally sourced fish and lamb dishes. Expect to pay around 4,000–6,000 ISK per person for a main and drink.

day_by_day.notes: Given the very early arrival and long drive, keep Day 1 light. Confirm your rental car booking in advance and download the Veður app (Icelandic Met Office) for real-time weather and aurora forecasts. January days are very short — expect only 4–5 hours of usable daylight, so the drive north will be partly in darkness. Drive carefully on potentially icy roads; studded tyres are standard on winter rentals.

day_by_day.morning: After a good night's rest, enjoy a hotel breakfast at Siglunes. Then visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) on the harbour — one of Iceland's finest regional museums. Explore three beautifully restored buildings documenting Siglufjörður's golden age as the herring capital of the North Atlantic. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the short distance (approximately 25 minutes) south through the tunnel to Hofsós village and visit the legendary Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool. Perched dramatically on a cliff edge overlooking Skagafjörður fjord, this geothermal pool is widely considered Iceland's most beautiful. Soak in the 38–40°C water while gazing across the fjord — a truly restorative experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður as darkness falls. Join the guided Northern Lights Hunting tour departing from Siglufjörður — your guide will drive to optimal dark-sky locations around the fjords away from any light pollution, maximising your chances of seeing the aurora borealis. Tours typically run 21:00–midnight.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast included or available — enjoy skyr, rye bread, smoked salmon, and Icelandic dairy products.
meals.lunch: Café Rauðka in Siglufjörður — a charming local café serving homemade soups, sandwiches, and cakes. Budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Sigló Hótel restaurant or a simple self-catered meal from the local Samkaup supermarket — pick up skyr, bread, cheese, and smoked lamb for a cosy in-room dinner around 2,000–3,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: The Herring Era Museum may have reduced winter hours — check ahead and book tickets online (around 2,500 ISK per adult). Hofsós pool entry is approximately 1,000–1,200 ISK; bring your own towel or rent one on site. The northern lights tour should be booked in advance through your hotel or a local operator; cost is typically 8,000–12,000 ISK per person. Aurora activity depends on clear skies and solar activity — the KP index app is useful.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, prepare for the Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike. Drive through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel (free, approximately 10 minutes from Siglufjörður) and park at the tunnel exit on the Héðinsfjörður side. Hike into the hauntingly beautiful, completely uninhabited fjord — explore the ruins of the abandoned farmsteads of Heiðarbær and Hólsárbær, deserted in the 1950s. The flat valley floor makes for easy winter walking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return through the tunnel and warm up with a hot drink back in Siglufjörður. Spend the afternoon exploring the town on foot — visit the small Folk Music Centre (Þjóðlagasetur), browse the harbour area, and walk along the snow-dusted streets of this perfectly preserved herring-era town. Pop into the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) for a warm geothermal soak.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at Hannes Boy or try the Sigló Hótel restaurant for a more upscale experience. Afterward, keep an eye on the aurora forecast — if conditions look promising, drive back through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel for a self-guided dark-sky viewing session away from town lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or self-catered — Icelandic oatmeal porridge with skyr and berries from the supermarket.
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of hot soup and sandwiches for the hike — prepare the night before using supermarket supplies. Budget around 1,000–1,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant — try the pan-fried Arctic char or the lamb fillet. Budget around 4,500–6,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Héðinsfjörður hike is approximately 4–6 km return and relatively flat, but dress in full winter layers — waterproof jacket, thermal base layers, wool mid-layer, hat, gloves, and waterproof boots with good grip. January temperatures can drop to -5°C or lower with wind chill. The fjord is completely uninhabited so carry a charged phone and let someone know your plans. The local swimming pool costs around 900–1,100 ISK.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Siglufjörður through the tunnels to Sauðárkrókur (approximately 45 minutes), the largest town in Skagafjörður. Visit the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum (Byggðasafn Skagfirðinga) to learn about the region's Viking-age history, horse culture, and turf farmhouse heritage. The museum complex includes the beautifully preserved Glaumbær turf farm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to explore the Skagafjörður valley — drive to Varmahlíð and visit the Víðimýri turf church, one of Iceland's oldest and most photogenic historic churches, dating to 1834. The surrounding snow-covered landscape in January is extraordinarily atmospheric. Return to Siglufjörður via the scenic coastal road through Hofsós.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Siglufjörður, enjoy a quiet evening. Try cooking a simple Icelandic meal in your hotel room if facilities allow, or head to Café Rauðka for a lighter evening meal. Check the aurora forecast and, if skies are clear, take a short drive to the dark fjord shore for aurora watching.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Café Áslaug in Sauðárkrókur — a local favourite serving traditional Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa) and fresh bread. Budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered or Café Rauðka — pick up fresh skyr, smoked lamb, rye bread, and Icelandic butter from the supermarket for a budget-friendly evening. Budget around 1,500–2,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær turf farm and the Heritage Museum have limited winter hours — verify opening times before visiting (entry approximately 2,000 ISK). Víðimýri church is typically accessible year-round from the outside even if the interior is closed in winter. Roads between Siglufjörður and Sauðárkrókur are generally well-maintained but check road conditions at road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east from Siglufjörður along the spectacular Tröllaskagi coastal road (Route 76) toward Ólafsfjörður and then south to Dalvík (approximately 1 hour). Embark on the Tröllaskagi Peninsula Whale Watching & Sea Safari — winter departures offer the chance to spot humpback whales, minke whales, white-beaked dolphins, and harbour porpoises in the rich waters of Eyjafjörður. Tours typically depart at 09:00 or 10:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the sea safari (approximately 3 hours on the water), warm up in Dalvík with a hot lunch. Explore the small Hvoll Museum in Dalvík, which houses a fascinating exhibit on the 'Dalvík Giant' — a local man of extraordinary height — alongside natural history displays. Drive back toward Siglufjörður via Ólafsfjörður.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for a well-earned rest. Dine at the Sigló Hótel restaurant for a slightly more indulgent mid-trip meal — try the pan-seared cod with Icelandic butter sauce or the slow-cooked lamb shank. Check aurora conditions before bed.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the drive to Dalvík.
meals.lunch: Gísli, Eiríkur, Helgi restaurant in Dalvík — a beloved local spot known for hearty fish and chips and Icelandic comfort food. Budget around 3,000–4,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Sigló Hótel restaurant — a step up in quality for a mid-trip treat. Budget around 6,000–9,000 ISK per person with a glass of wine.

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching tours from Dalvík or Ólafsfjörður cost approximately 10,000–12,000 ISK per adult — book in advance through Arctic Sea Tours or a similar operator. Dress in the warmest layers you have for the boat; the sea wind is biting in January. Sickness bags are provided but consider seasickness tablets if you are prone. The Hvoll Museum entry is around 1,000 ISK.

day_by_day.morning: Take a slower morning — sleep in slightly and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Then take a self-guided winter photography walk around Siglufjörður harbour and the surrounding snow-covered hillsides. The dramatic fjord scenery, colourful fishing boats, and snow-capped peaks make for stunning winter photography even in low January light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south to Hofsós again for a second, more leisurely visit to the Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool — this time with no rush. Spend 1.5–2 hours soaking and relaxing. Afterward, visit the Icelandic Emigration Centre (Vesturfarasetrið) in Hofsós, which tells the fascinating story of the 16,000 Icelanders who emigrated to North America in the 19th century.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Join the Northern Lights Hunting guided tour again if you missed the aurora on previous attempts, or self-drive to a dark location along the fjord. The more attempts you make, the better your chances across a 13-day trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — take your time and enjoy.
meals.lunch: Café Rauðka in Siglufjörður — homemade soup and fresh-baked bread. Budget around 2,000–3,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner — visit the Samkaup supermarket and prepare a simple pasta or rice dish with Icelandic smoked lamb or tinned fish. Budget around 1,500–2,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: The Icelandic Emigration Centre in Hofsós has a genealogy database — if you have Icelandic heritage, this is a wonderful place to research your roots. Entry is approximately 1,500 ISK. This is a good rest-and-recharge day mid-trip. Use the evening to review your photos, plan remaining days, and check the aurora forecast carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east from Siglufjörður through the tunnels and south to Akureyri (approximately 1 hour 15 minutes) — Iceland's second city and the capital of the north. Explore the charming town centre: visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill, stroll the pedestrianised Hafnarstræti shopping street, and browse the Akureyri Art Museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's northernmost botanical garden, beautiful even in winter with its snow-covered grounds. Then head to the Akureyri Swimming Pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar) — a superb geothermal facility with multiple hot pots, a steam room, and a large outdoor pool. A perfect mid-trip soak.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Akureyri before returning to Siglufjörður. Akureyri has the best restaurant selection in northern Iceland — try Strikið restaurant for elevated Icelandic cuisine with panoramic fjord views, or Rub23 for excellent sushi and grilled meats.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing.
meals.lunch: Bláa Kannan café in Akureyri — a beloved institution in a historic building, serving excellent coffee, cakes, and light lunches. Budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Strikið restaurant, Akureyri — panoramic views, excellent Icelandic lamb and fish dishes. Budget around 5,500–8,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri Swimming Pool entry is approximately 1,000–1,200 ISK. The drive back to Siglufjörður from Akureyri takes about 1 hour 15 minutes — plan to leave Akureyri by 20:00 at the latest to return safely. Akureyri has a Bónus supermarket if you need to stock up on supplies. Parking in Akureyri town centre is generally free in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Siglufjörður to the Mývatn region (approximately 2 hours via Akureyri and Route 1 east). Begin at the Námaskarð geothermal area (Hverir) — a surreal, Mars-like landscape of boiling mud pots, steaming fumaroles, and vivid orange and yellow sulphur deposits. Walk the marked paths carefully — the ground is extremely hot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a stunning geothermal lagoon set against the volcanic landscape of the Mývatn region. The milky blue-green water is rich in minerals and maintained at 36–40°C. Spend 1.5–2 hours soaking in one of Iceland's finest hot spring experiences outside the Golden Circle.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Siglufjörður (approximately 2 hours). Stop for dinner in Akureyri on the way back, or pick up supplies for a self-catered dinner at the hotel. Check aurora conditions — the Mývatn area has very dark skies and is an excellent aurora-viewing location if you choose to stay later.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the drive.
meals.lunch: Café Sel at the Mývatn Nature Baths — serves Icelandic lamb soup, sandwiches, and hot drinks. Budget around 2,500–4,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Greifinn restaurant in Akureyri on the return journey — a reliable mid-range option with pizza, pasta, and Icelandic mains. Budget around 3,500–5,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn Nature Baths entry is approximately 6,500–7,500 ISK per adult — book online in advance as it can be busy even in winter. Bring your swimsuit and a towel (rentals available). The Námaskarð area is free to visit but stay strictly on marked paths. This is a long driving day — approximately 4 hours total — so start early and drive carefully on potentially icy Route 1.

day_by_day.morning: A dedicated rest and recovery morning. Sleep in, enjoy a long hotel breakfast, and spend time reading, journalling, or reviewing your photos from the trip so far. Take a short, gentle walk along the Siglufjörður harbour front to breathe the crisp Arctic air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Music Centre (Þjóðlagasetur) — a small but fascinating museum dedicated to Icelandic folk music and the rimur poetic tradition. Afterward, explore the town's small independent shops and pick up Icelandic souvenirs — local wool products, dried fish, and Icelandic sea salt make excellent gifts. Visit the local bakery for fresh kleinur (Icelandic doughnuts).
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Northern Lights Hunting guided tour from Siglufjörður for another attempt at the aurora. Your guide will monitor forecasts in real time and drive to the best available dark-sky location. Afterward, warm up with a hot chocolate or Brennivín (Icelandic schnapps) back at the hotel bar.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Local bakery in Siglufjörður — fresh bread, kleinur, and coffee. Budget around 1,000–1,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant — a final visit to this local favourite. Try the fish soup starter followed by the catch of the day. Budget around 4,500–6,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is an intentional slow day to prevent travel fatigue on a 13-day trip. Use the afternoon to do laundry if needed (ask the hotel), charge all devices, and plan the final days of the itinerary. The Folk Music Centre entry is approximately 1,000–1,500 ISK.

day_by_day.morning: Drive north along the coast from Siglufjörður toward the end of the Tröllaskagi Peninsula — explore the dramatic coastal scenery around Skagaströnd and the remote northern headlands. Stop at viewpoints overlooking the Arctic Ocean and look for seabirds including eider ducks, fulmars, and ravens along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return south and visit the Skagafjörður valley again, this time focusing on the horse farms of the region — Skagafjörður is the heartland of the Icelandic horse. Many farms offer short winter riding experiences or at minimum allow you to meet and photograph these beautiful, thick-maned horses in their snowy paddocks. Contact Hestasport or Lýtingsstaðir farm in advance to arrange a visit.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Self-catered dinner using fresh ingredients from the supermarket — try making a simple Icelandic fish stew (plokkfiskur) with cod, potatoes, onion, and béchamel sauce. Check aurora conditions and step outside periodically throughout the evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos and sandwiches for the coastal drive — self-catered from supermarket supplies. Budget around 1,000–1,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered plokkfiskur (Icelandic fish stew) — ingredients from Samkaup supermarket. Budget around 2,000–2,500 ISK for a hearty meal.

day_by_day.notes: Icelandic horse riding in winter costs approximately 8,000–15,000 ISK per person depending on the length of the ride — book at least a day in advance. Even a 1-hour walk with the horses is a memorable experience. The coastal road north of Siglufjörður can be icy and narrow — drive with extreme caution and check road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Akureyri and take the ferry across Eyjafjörður to Hrísey island (approximately 15 minutes crossing) — Iceland's second-largest island and a peaceful, car-free haven. Walk the island's marked trails through the snow, spot ptarmigan (Iceland's most common bird in winter), and enjoy the extraordinary silence and Arctic atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return by ferry to the mainland and drive south from Akureyri toward Goðafoss waterfall (approximately 45 minutes east on Route 1). Even in January, Goðafoss — the 'Waterfall of the Gods' — is spectacular, with ice formations building up around its edges and the powerful glacial water thundering over the horseshoe-shaped falls. A short, easy walk from the car park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Enjoy dinner at the Sigló Hótel restaurant for a relaxed, quality evening meal. This is one of your last full evenings — savour the atmosphere of this remarkable Arctic town.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before the early drive.
meals.lunch: Bring packed lunch for Hrísey island — there are very limited food options on the island in winter. Alternatively, eat at a café in Akureyri before the ferry. Budget around 2,000–3,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Sigló Hótel restaurant — try the lamb tenderloin or the pan-fried halibut. Budget around 6,000–8,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Hrísey ferry departs from Árskógssandur (approximately 30 minutes south of Akureyri) — check the Sævar ferry timetable in advance as winter schedules are reduced. Ferry costs approximately 1,500–2,000 ISK return. Goðafoss is free to visit and accessible year-round. The paths around the waterfall can be icy — wear crampons or ice grips (available cheaply at Icelandic hardware stores or outdoor shops).

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — begin with a meaningful return to the Héðinsfjörður abandoned village for a longer, more contemplative hike. With nearly two weeks of acclimatisation to the landscape and cold, you can now fully appreciate the haunting beauty of this deserted fjord. Explore further into the valley than on your first visit, reaching the old farmstead ruins at the far end.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siglufjörður and spend the afternoon at the Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool one final time — a perfect way to reflect on the trip. Soak in the geothermal waters, gaze across the fjord, and let the mineral-rich water ease any hiking fatigue. Afterward, drive back to Siglufjörður and begin packing.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Hannes Boy restaurant — order generously and celebrate an extraordinary 13-day Arctic adventure. Share stories with fellow travellers or the friendly local staff. After dinner, make one final aurora attempt — step outside and look up. January in Siglufjörður offers some of the darkest skies in Iceland.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of hot soup and rye bread sandwiches for the Héðinsfjörður hike.
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant — farewell dinner. Order the full experience: fish soup starter, Arctic char or lamb main, and skyr dessert with Icelandic cream. Budget around 5,000–7,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Use the afternoon packing session to ensure you are within airline baggage limits — Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa) and other souvenirs add weight quickly. Return your rental car fuel tank full to avoid refuelling charges. Set multiple alarms for the early morning departure drive.

day_by_day.morning: Early wake-up and final hotel checkout. Enjoy a quick hotel breakfast or grab coffee and a pastry to go. Begin the drive south from Siglufjörður toward Keflavík International Airport (approximately 5–5.5 hours). Drive carefully on winter roads — allow extra time for icy conditions, especially in the first hour through the tunnels and mountain passes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavík Airport with ample time before your departure. Return the rental car at the airport car rental facility. Check in, clear security, and browse the Duty Free store — Icelandic wool products, Brennivín, Skyr chocolate, and Icelandic sea salt are excellent last-minute purchases at competitive duty-free prices.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in the Arctic north — the dancing northern lights, the steaming geothermal pools, the haunted abandoned fjords, the thundering waterfalls, and the warm hospitality of Siglufjörður's small but vibrant community.

meals.breakfast: Quick hotel breakfast or coffee and pastry to go — budget around 1,000–1,500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café at Keflavík — Icelandic lamb soup or a smoked salmon bagel for a final taste of Iceland. Budget around 3,000–4,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: On-board flight meal or airport dining before departure.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 5.5 hours for the drive from Siglufjörður to Keflavík in winter conditions — do not underestimate this. Check road.is one final time before departing. If your flight is in the late afternoon or evening, you could make a brief stop at the Blue Lagoon (pre-booking essential, approximately 15 minutes from the airport) for a final geothermal soak before flying home — a classic Icelandic send-off. Budget around 8,000–12,000 ISK for Blue Lagoon entry.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður
experiences.description: Join a guided northern lights tour departing from Siglufjörður, venturing into the dark fjordside countryside away from light pollution. The remote location of Siglufjörður in northern Iceland makes it one of the best spots in the country to witness the aurora borealis dancing over the fjord and surrounding mountains.

experiences.name: Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool
experiences.description: Visit the stunning Hofsós swimming pool, often called Iceland's most beautiful geothermal pool, perched on a cliff edge overlooking Skagafjörður fjord. A short scenic drive from Siglufjörður, this geothermally heated outdoor pool offers breathtaking panoramic views of the fjord and distant mountains, especially magical at sunset or under the northern lights.

experiences.name: Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike
experiences.description: Explore the hauntingly beautiful and completely uninhabited Héðinsfjörður fjord, accessible via a short tunnel from Siglufjörður. Hike through this remote valley to discover the ruins of an abandoned fishing village, dramatic waterfalls, and pristine Arctic nature. The fjord is surrounded by towering peaks and offers exceptional wildlife spotting including Arctic foxes and seabirds.

experiences.name: Herring Era Museum & Local Culture Experience
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Siglufjörður's rich cultural heritage at the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið), one of Iceland's finest regional museums. Explore restored warehouses and boats that tell the story of the great herring boom of the early 20th century. Pair the visit with a meal at a local restaurant sampling traditional Icelandic fish dishes and lamb soup.

experiences.name: Tröllaskagi Peninsula Whale Watching & Sea Safari
experiences.description: Embark on a sea safari from the nearby town of Dalvík or Ólafsfjörður, exploring the rich marine waters of Eyjafjörður — one of Iceland's longest fjords. These waters are home to humpback whales, minke whales, white-beaked dolphins, and harbour porpoises. The dramatic mountain scenery of the Tröllaskagi Peninsula provides a stunning backdrop for this unforgettable Arctic wildlife experience.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage, then transfer via pre-arranged luxury private car service northward toward Siglufjörður — a scenic 4–5 hour drive through the Icelandic highlands and along the Tröllaskagi Peninsula. Enjoy the dramatic winter landscape from the warmth of your chauffeured vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður mid-afternoon. Check in and settle into your premium room overlooking the fjord. Take a gentle, self-guided stroll along the harbour front to orient yourself with the charming, colourful fishing village. Breathe the crisp Arctic air and watch the last traces of the brief winter daylight fade over the snow-dusted mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a quiet, indulgent dinner at the hotel restaurant, sampling locally sourced Icelandic fish and lamb. Retire early to prepare for the adventures ahead.

meals.breakfast: Light refreshments on board the flight or at Keflavík airport's premium lounge (Saga Lounge if flying Icelandair Business)
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch box arranged by the hotel driver, or stop at Blönduós for a warm meal at a local café en route
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Siglunes restaurant — expect pan-seared Arctic char, slow-roasted lamb shank, and Skyr-based desserts paired with Icelandic craft beer or fine wine

day_by_day.notes: Sunrise in Siglufjörður in mid-January is around 11:30 and sunset around 15:30, giving only about 4 hours of daylight. The drive from Keflavík is approximately 400 km; ensure the private transfer is pre-booked. Road conditions in January can be challenging — confirm Route 76 through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel is open.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast at the hotel, visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's finest regional museums. Explore three beautifully restored warehouse buildings chronicling Siglufjörður's golden age as the herring capital of the North Atlantic. Engage with interactive exhibits, vintage fishing equipment, and evocative period reconstructions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a guided walk through Siglufjörður's historic old town with a local cultural guide arranged through the hotel. Visit the charming wooden church, the old merchant houses, and the harbour piers. Stop for hot cocoa or Icelandic coffee at a local café. In the late afternoon, visit the small but excellent Folk Music Centre (Þjóðlagasetur) to experience traditional Icelandic music.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður — join a guided aurora tour departing from the hotel. Your expert guide will drive you into the dark fjordside countryside away from any light pollution, monitoring aurora forecasts in real time. Wrap up in provided thermal suits and sip hot chocolate under the stars while waiting for the Kp-index to deliver a display of the Northern Lights.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — smoked salmon, skyr with berries, rye bread, soft-boiled eggs, and fresh coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Kaffi Rauðka, Siglufjörður's beloved local café — hearty fish soup, open-faced sandwiches, and homemade cakes
meals.dinner: Pre-tour early dinner at Hotel Siglunes — warming lamb stew or pan-fried cod with root vegetables before the evening aurora excursion

day_by_day.notes: The Herring Era Museum may have limited winter hours — confirm opening times in advance (typically 13:00–17:00 in January). The Northern Lights tour typically runs 21:00–00:00. Aurora activity depends on geomagnetic conditions; the guide will reschedule if cloud cover is total. Dress in multiple thermal layers.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along the scenic Route 76 to Hofsós (approximately 45 minutes), one of Iceland's oldest trading posts. Upon arrival, visit the Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool — perched dramatically on a cliff edge above Skagafjörður, this geothermal pool is widely regarded as Iceland's most beautiful. Soak in the 38–40°C mineral-rich waters while gazing across the fjord to snow-capped mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Hofsós on foot. Visit the Icelandic Emigration Centre (Vesturfarasetrið), which tells the story of the 19th-century Icelandic emigration to North America — a surprisingly moving and well-curated museum. Browse the small local craft shop for artisan Icelandic woolens and ceramics. Return to Siglufjörður in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium spa evening at Hotel Siglunes. Arrange a hot tub session overlooking the fjord, followed by an in-room massage if available through the hotel's concierge. Dine in the hotel restaurant with a focus on the evening's tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — freshly baked pastries, Icelandic cheese board, smoked meats, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Hofsós — bring a premium picnic prepared by the hotel, or dine at the small local guesthouse café if open in winter
meals.dinner: Tasting menu dinner at Hotel Siglunes — multi-course experience featuring seasonal Icelandic ingredients: langoustine bisque, reindeer carpaccio, and volcanic salt-crusted lamb

day_by_day.notes: The Hofsós pool is open year-round but confirm winter hours (often 07:00–21:00). Bring your own swimwear or rent on-site. The drive along Route 76 is stunning but can be icy in January — drive carefully or arrange a local driver. The Emigration Centre may have reduced winter hours.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the Héðinsfjörður Abandoned Village Hike — one of the most hauntingly beautiful experiences in northern Iceland. Drive through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel (Route 76) and enter the completely uninhabited fjord. With a local guide, hike through the snow-covered landscape to the ruins of the abandoned farmsteads, learning the story of the last families who left in 1951. The silence and isolation are profound.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Héðinsfjörður at a leisurely pace. Your guide will point out Arctic fox tracks, frozen waterfalls, and the dramatic geology of the fjord walls. Enjoy a thermos of hot soup and gourmet sandwiches prepared by the hotel as a wilderness lunch. Return through the tunnel to Siglufjörður by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Second Northern Lights Hunting opportunity from Siglufjörður. If last night's tour was clouded out, tonight offers another chance. Alternatively, if you witnessed the aurora on Day 2, spend the evening at the hotel's bar sampling Icelandic spirits — try Brennivín (Black Death schnapps) and local craft gins — while the hotel staff share stories of life in this remote Arctic town.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast at Hotel Siglunes to fuel the hike — porridge with brown sugar and cream, eggs, bacon, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed wilderness lunch prepared by the hotel — thermos of lamb soup, artisan rye bread with smoked salmon, Skyr with granola, and hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Siglunes — grilled Atlantic halibut with beurre blanc, roasted root vegetables, and a selection from the Icelandic wine and spirits menu

day_by_day.notes: The Héðinsfjörður hike is moderate in summer but can be strenuous in winter snow. Wear waterproof hiking boots with crampons or microspikes. The guide is essential as the terrain can be disorienting in low light. Total hike distance is approximately 6–8 km return. Daylight window is narrow — begin no later than 11:00.

day_by_day.morning: Tröllaskagi Peninsula Whale Watching & Sea Safari — depart early by private transfer to Dalvík or Ólafsfjörður (approximately 30–45 minutes south). Board a premium small-group sea safari vessel equipped with heated cabins. Explore the rich marine waters of Eyjafjörður, one of Iceland's longest fjords, in search of humpback whales, minke whales, white-beaked dolphins, and harbour porpoises that frequent these waters year-round.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to shore after the sea safari. Explore the small town of Dalvík briefly — visit the quirky Byggðasafnið Hvoll museum, which houses an exhibit on the largest man ever born in Iceland. Drive back to Siglufjörður along the scenic coastal road, stopping at viewpoints over the Tröllaskagi Peninsula's dramatic mountain ridges.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at Hotel Siglunes. Enjoy a long, indulgent soak in the hotel's outdoor hot tub under the Arctic sky. Dine at the hotel with a focus on the freshest catch of the day — your whale watching guide may have recommended what the local fishermen brought in this morning.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — smoked trout, rye crispbread, soft cheeses, and fresh fruit before the early departure
meals.lunch: Warm lunch on board the sea safari vessel (hot soup and sandwiches typically provided) or at a Dalvík restaurant post-tour
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Siglunes — fresh-caught fish of the day, perhaps pan-seared wolffish or monkfish, with a premium Icelandic craft beer pairing

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching in January is excellent in Eyjafjörður — this fjord has some of the highest year-round whale sighting rates in Iceland. Dress in full waterproof gear; the sea safari company provides outer suits. Book the premium small-group tour in advance. Sea conditions can occasionally cancel tours — have a backup plan.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the hotel. Sleep in and enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast. Spend the morning in the hotel's lounge reading, journaling, or simply watching the winter light slowly illuminate the fjord. This is a deliberate rest day built into the itinerary to allow for recovery and spontaneous exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Self-guided photography walk around Siglufjörður during the precious few hours of daylight. The town's colourful wooden houses, snow-covered rooftops, and dramatic fjord backdrop make for extraordinary winter photography. Visit the small harbour and watch local fishermen at work. Pop into any open local shops for Icelandic wool products, local honey, or handmade crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður — third opportunity. Siglufjörður's position deep in a fjord with minimal light pollution makes it one of the best bases in Iceland for aurora viewing. Tonight, venture further afield with your guide to a high-elevation viewpoint above the town for a panoramic aurora perspective if conditions allow.

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — the full spread, enjoyed slowly with extra coffee and the morning's Icelandic news
meals.lunch: Lunch at Kaffi Rauðka — the town's beloved café, known for its homemade soups, cakes, and warm atmosphere
meals.dinner: Early dinner at Hotel Siglunes before the aurora tour — Icelandic lamb burger with truffle fries, or a warming beef and root vegetable casserole

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to catch up on rest, especially if jet lag or the previous days' activities have been tiring. The photography walk is best done between 11:30 and 15:00 when the low winter sun casts golden-hour light almost all day. Check aurora forecasts on vedur.is or the My Aurora Forecast app.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Akureyri — Iceland's 'Capital of the North' (approximately 1 hour south via Route 82 and Route 1). Depart after breakfast and arrive in time to explore this charming city. Visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched above the town, then stroll the pedestrianised Hafnarstræti shopping street. Browse the excellent Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri) for contemporary Icelandic art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Akureyri's culinary and cultural scene. Visit the Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's northernmost botanical garden, magical in winter snow. Browse the excellent local bookshops and design stores. Visit the Akureyri Museum for regional history. Depart for Siglufjörður in the late afternoon to return before dark.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner out at one of Akureyri's finest restaurants before the return drive, or return to Siglufjörður for a hotel dinner. Spend the evening in the hotel's lounge with Icelandic spirits and live music if available.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Rub23 in Akureyri — one of Iceland's most acclaimed restaurants outside Reykjavík, known for its exceptional sushi and grilled meats with Japanese-Nordic fusion
meals.dinner: Dinner at Strikið restaurant in Akureyri (panoramic fjord views, excellent lamb and seafood) before the return drive, or back at Hotel Siglunes

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is approximately 75 km from Siglufjörður. The drive via Route 82 along the Tröllaskagi coast is scenic but can be icy — allow extra time. Alternatively, take the faster Route 1 via Ólafsfjörður tunnel. Akureyri has excellent shopping for premium Icelandic design goods, wool, and local food products.

day_by_day.morning: Guided snowshoeing or winter hiking excursion in the mountains above Siglufjörður. The town is surrounded by dramatic peaks that offer extraordinary winter wilderness experiences. With a certified mountain guide, ascend into the snow-covered highlands above the fjord for sweeping panoramic views of the surrounding peninsula and distant mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a warming lunch. Spend the afternoon at leisure — arrange an in-room spa treatment through the hotel concierge, or visit the local geothermal swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) for a quintessentially Icelandic hot pot experience alongside locals.
day_by_day.evening: Special premium dinner experience at Hotel Siglunes — request the chef's table or a private dining arrangement if available. Pair a multi-course Icelandic tasting menu with a curated wine flight. Toast the halfway point of your extraordinary Arctic journey.

meals.breakfast: Hearty pre-hike breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — oatmeal with Icelandic honey, eggs any style, smoked salmon, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Post-hike warming lunch at the hotel — thick lamb soup with fresh bread, followed by Skyr cheesecake
meals.dinner: Chef's table or premium tasting menu at Hotel Siglunes — seven courses showcasing the best of Icelandic seasonal produce, paired with wines selected by the hotel sommelier

day_by_day.notes: The snowshoeing excursion requires advance booking through the hotel or a local guide service. Avalanche risk is a consideration in the mountains above Siglufjörður in January — only go with a certified guide who checks conditions. The local swimming pool is a wonderful cultural experience and costs only a few hundred ISK.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Varmahlíð in Skagafjörður valley (approximately 1 hour south) for a unique winter experience. Visit the Glaumbær turf farm museum — one of Iceland's best-preserved historic turf farmsteads, offering a fascinating glimpse into how Icelanders lived for centuries. The snow-covered turf roofs in winter are particularly photogenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Skagafjörður region, known as Iceland's horse country. Visit a premium Icelandic horse farm for a private stable tour and, if conditions allow, a short winter riding experience on the famous five-gaited Icelandic horse. Return to Siglufjörður via the scenic coastal route in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting from Siglufjörður — fourth opportunity. By now you will have developed a rhythm with the aurora tours and know the best local spots. Alternatively, if aurora activity has been excellent on previous nights, spend this evening at the hotel enjoying a private hot tub session under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before the day trip
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Áss in Varmahlíð — a charming local café known for homemade soups, cakes, and Icelandic coffee culture
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Siglunes — slow-roasted Icelandic lamb shoulder with root vegetable gratin and red wine reduction, paired with a robust Icelandic red ale

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær turf farm has limited winter hours — confirm in advance. The Icelandic horse farm visit should be pre-arranged through the hotel concierge. Skagafjörður is one of the most important horse-breeding regions in Iceland and the horses are exceptionally well-cared for. The drive back via Route 75 along the fjord is beautiful in winter light.

day_by_day.morning: Return visit to Hofsós Infinity Hot Spring Pool for a second, more leisurely soak — this time perhaps at opening time when the pool is quietest and the morning light (arriving around 11:30) creates a magical atmosphere over the fjord. Spend a full two hours in the geothermal waters, alternating between the main pool and the cold plunge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Skagafjörður coastline on the return journey. Stop at the dramatic sea cliffs and bird colonies near Málmey island viewpoint. Visit the small fishing village of Sauðárkrókur — the largest town in Skagafjörður — for a brief exploration of its harbour and local shops. Return to Siglufjörður by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a cultural evening in Siglufjörður if available — the Folk Music Centre occasionally hosts traditional Icelandic music performances. Alternatively, arrange a private guided stargazing session above the town with a local astronomy enthusiast, learning about the Arctic night sky and the science of the Northern Lights.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — lighter fare today, fresh fruit, yoghurt, and pastries before the hot spring visit
meals.lunch: Lunch in Sauðárkrókur at Kaffi Krókur — local fish and chips, lamb soup, or the daily special in a cosy setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Siglunes — pan-seared scallops with cauliflower purée, followed by slow-cooked beef cheek with Icelandic barley risotto

day_by_day.notes: The Hofsós pool is magical in the early morning light of an Icelandic winter — the low sun angle creates extraordinary reflections on the water. Sauðárkrókur has a small but good selection of shops and is worth a brief stop. Check the Folk Music Centre's winter programme in advance through the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Tröllaskagi Peninsula's interior. With a private 4WD guide, venture into the mountain passes and hidden valleys of this dramatic peninsula. Visit frozen waterfalls, cross snow-covered highland plateaus, and experience the raw, untouched wilderness that makes this region one of Iceland's most spectacular yet least-visited areas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the 4WD wilderness excursion. Stop at a remote mountain viewpoint for a thermos lunch overlooking the fjords below. Your guide will share knowledge of the local geology, wildlife, and the Norse mythology associated with the trolls said to inhabit these mountains. Return to Siglufjörður by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights Hunting opportunity from Siglufjörður. Make this evening special — bring a bottle of Champagne to toast under the aurora if it appears. Your guide will take you to the most remote and dramatic viewpoint discovered during the trip for a fitting finale to your aurora hunting experiences.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast at Hotel Siglunes to fuel the full-day excursion
meals.lunch: Gourmet wilderness picnic prepared by the hotel — premium thermos of seafood chowder, artisan sandwiches, Icelandic chocolate, and hot coffee in the mountains
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Hotel Siglunes — request the best table with fjord views, order the premium tasting menu, and open a bottle of fine Champagne or Burgundy

day_by_day.notes: The Tröllaskagi interior 4WD excursion must be booked through a specialist local operator — the hotel concierge can arrange this. A super-jeep or modified 4WD is essential for winter mountain travel. This is one of the most exclusive and memorable experiences available in the region. Dress in maximum thermal layers.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Siglufjörður. Take a slow, reflective walk along the harbour in the pre-dawn darkness, watching the fishing boats prepare for the day. As the brief winter light arrives around 11:30, photograph the town one last time — the colourful houses, the snow-capped peaks, the mirror-still fjord. Visit any shops you haven't yet explored for last-minute gifts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Hotel Siglunes and begin the private transfer south toward Reykjavík (approximately 5–6 hours). Stop en route at Blönduós for a coffee break. Continue south through the dramatic Icelandic interior landscape, passing through Borgarnes and along the Hvalfjörður fjord road for a scenic final approach to the capital.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Reykjavík and check into a premium city hotel (The Retreat at Blue Lagoon, Hotel Borg, or ION Adventure Hotel — pre-book separately). Enjoy a celebratory final dinner at one of Reykjavík's finest restaurants, reflecting on 12 extraordinary days in the Arctic north.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — savour every bite of the smoked salmon, fresh bread, and strong Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Stop at a premium restaurant in Borgarnes — Borgarnes Settlement Centre café offers excellent Icelandic lamb soup and traditional dishes
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dill Restaurant in Reykjavík (Iceland's only Michelin-starred restaurant) — a New Nordic tasting menu celebrating Icelandic ingredients at the highest level; advance reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time at Hotel Siglunes is typically 11:00 — arrange a late check-out if needed given the brief morning daylight. The drive to Reykjavík via the scenic Hvalfjörður road adds only 20 minutes but is far more beautiful than the tunnel. Dill Restaurant requires reservations weeks in advance — book before the trip begins.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. If staying near the Blue Lagoon, enjoy a premium early morning soak in the world-famous geothermal lagoon — book the Retreat Spa package for the most exclusive experience, including private changing facilities, in-water treatments, and access to the exclusive Retreat Lagoon. Alternatively, explore Reykjavík's Old Harbour and Harpa Concert Hall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Keflavík International Airport via private transfer (approximately 45 minutes from Reykjavík, 20 minutes from Blue Lagoon). Allow ample time for check-in and security. Browse the duty-free shops for Icelandic spirits, chocolate, and skincare products. Relax in the Saga Lounge before boarding.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland on your return Icelandair flight, carrying memories of the Northern Lights dancing over Siglufjörður, the silence of Héðinsfjörður, the warmth of geothermal pools under Arctic skies, and the extraordinary privilege of 13 days in one of the world's most remote and beautiful corners.

meals.breakfast: Premium breakfast at the hotel or at the Blue Lagoon Retreat's exclusive dining area — smoked fish, Skyr, fresh pastries, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Keflavík Airport's Saga Lounge or a final meal at a Reykjavík restaurant before airport transfer
meals.dinner: In-flight dining on Icelandair (Saga Class if booked) or dinner at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon must be booked well in advance — the Retreat package sells out months ahead. Arrive at Keflavík Airport at least 2.5 hours before departure. Iceland's duty-free is excellent value — Brennivín, Icelandic gin, Nói Síríus chocolate, and Bioeffect skincare are top picks. Confirm return transfer booking the night before.

query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January
